extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists, mathematicians working with graded modules/resolutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the SINGULAR procedure grtranspose1 (from gradedModules.lib): signature, assumptions about its input, and example usage showing it computes the graded transpose of a graded object / chain complex. Intended to guide users invoking the routine on resolutions or graded objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure source / context
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure from library gradedModules.lib (see Section D.15.18 [gradedModules lib], page 1960).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This routine is part of the gradedModules.lib library; examples and expected input types follow the library conventions for graded objects and chain complexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usage / signature
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: grtranspose1(M), graded object or list M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call signature expects a single argument M which should be a graded object or a list of graded objects (for example, a chain complex or a resolution). Example shown: LIB "gradedModules.lib"; ... list L = RR; list LLL = grtranspose1(L); grview(LLL);

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions on input
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume: M must be a graded object or a list of graded objects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure will not accept arbitrary non-graded inputs. Inputs are typically resolutions or graded module objects produced by other gradedModules.lib routines (e.g., outputs of grres, grobj, grview). Ensure the object has grading information (degrees) before calling grtranspose1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: same as input. Purpose: graded transpose of graded object or chain complex M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The routine returns a graded object (of the same structural type as the input) that is the graded transpose of the input chain complex/resolution. In examples, the transpose flips a resolution R <- ... into its graded transpose R(9)^2 <- ... etc., with adjusted degree shifts shown in grview output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example usage / expected output form
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: after computing a graded resolution L (via grres, grobj, etc.), calling list LLL = grtranspose1(L); grview(LLL) produces a Graded resolution with shifted degree notation (e.g., R(9)^2 <-- d_1 -- etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documentation includes a concrete example: construct a ring and ideal, compute I = grobj(groebner(J), intvec(0)), RR = grres(I,0,1), then L = RR and LLL = grtranspose1(L); grview(LLL) shows the graded-transposed resolution. Use this pattern to validate correct input and interpret the returned graded resolution.
